anchor_check.stage: scene-anchor check (D-015 rule 7, D-013 rule 2): the six anchors s03, s04, s15, s21, s28, s31, attempt 1 each
anchor_check.method: Each frame viewed whole at 720x1280, then ffmpeg crops of the 1440x2560 png (faces beside the sheet's front close-up or profile view, hands, cuffs, wrists, pockets, nostrils, ear lobes, props, number plates, signboard, cashbox, dashboard and the bottom band). Each png is an exact lanczos upscale of its 941x1672 raw (PSNR inf against the upscaled raw for all six), so detail is the raw's. Judged against shots.json (shot state, framing, refs, screen_direction, state_ledger, storyboard_notes), style.json (character and wardrobe locks for kiran, aditya, billu, mausi; negative_rules; style_frame; light_states; key_props), continuity.json via the state_ledger, and the refs kiran_p1, kiran_p2, kiran_hands, aditya, billu, mausi, pair_kiran_aditya_p1, pair_kiran_aditya_p2, pair_kiran_mausi_p2, bedroom_bed, lane_night, stairwell_up, car_forward, bureau_exterior, bureau_front, billu_car, key_bunch, brass_set. The warm grilled window in s04 and the marigold curtain in s31 belong to their own plates (lane_night, bureau_front). D-021's fallback is not triggered.
anchor_check.height_watch_D017: Not tested here: s15 has Aditya a step up and s28 has them at different depths. s34 is still the first same-depth test.
anchor_check.cuff_rule_D023_4_6: Both cuffs are at rest in every anchor that shows them (s03, s15, s28). No bare forearm near the scar's place and no scar anywhere.
not_checked: No face-matching tool was used. Identity and age are my judgement by eye from crops set beside the sheet close-ups.
Placement percentages are eye readings from the 720x1280 previews multiplied up, not pixel measurements.
Light direction was judged by eye.
Text: by eye on whole frames and on crops of plates, shutters, the signboard, the cashbox, the dashboard and the windows. I did not crop every part of every frame.
Only the s28 prompt was read (by grep). Every other verdict rests on the shots.json STATE, not on what that prompt said.
Camera moves and push-ins were not rendered, so whether a push crops anything into or out of the subtitle band was not checked.
D-021 decision 6 (the retake check of the regenerated sheets) is still unreported. I did not run it. pair_kiran_aditya_p1/p2 and pair_kiran_mausi_p2 were viewed only as whole sheets at 540x960.
The other 22 generated frames do not exist yet and were not judged.

frames.why_rejected: This is a side error on the prop the beat turns on: the hand and cuff over the scar (D-003, D-005). It breaks the s28 to s29 cut, and the henna disc on the back of a hand breaks a lock that Gate 3 fixed. s28 is also the anchor for s29 and s30, so its faults would spread (D-013 rule 2).
retake_fix: Cause: the prompt asks for both faces 'three-quarters to the camera', and the model turned both bodies to the camera to get it. Two people facing each other across the frame with their bodies square to the lens join his LEFT hand to her RIGHT.

Restage side-on, in picture terms. Aditya stands in profile facing the picture-right. His near shoulder, near arm and the patch pocket face the camera. The arm that reaches for her is the near one, on the camera side of his body. The watch wrist is hidden behind his body.

Kiran is turned to face the picture-left, side-on to the camera. The shoulder carrying the grey dupatta is the one nearer the camera. The hand he holds belongs to that same dupatta-side arm, on the near side, palm up or back up, with its red cuff at rest. Her face is in profile or near-profile with the nose to the picture-left, and the thin gold hoop shows on the near nostril.
Her other hand is hidden on the far side of her body (on the seat edge or the door frame behind her), not in her lap.
Write that the joined hands are nearer the camera than both bodies. Drop 'three-quarters to the camera' for both faces and use 'profile, turned slightly towards the camera' instead.
Add to the prompt's AVOID or FINAL CHECK: 'no henna disc on the back of either hand; the disc is only on a palm'.
If the retake still joins the wrong hands, accept the better take and log it (D-013 rule 11, D-023 rule 4.6's ladder). s29's macro then carries the hand side, as an insert made for it.
frames.waiting: s29 and s30 attach s28 and must not run until the s28 retake passes the retake check (D-023 rule 4.1).

frames.final_rule: D-013 rule 11 / D-023 rule 4.1: one retake per frame; attempt 2 is the better take and stands. No further retake. The anchor row's own fallback applies: 'If the retake still joins the wrong hands, accept the better take and log it ... s29's macro then carries the hand side.'
